title: Forecasting bridge damage within a predictive Structural Reliability-based DSS
authors: Francesca Brighenti, Mattia Francesco Bado, Francesco Romeo, Daniele Zonta

dataset: Real-world bridge inspection database from Autonomous Province of Trento (Italy) comprising reinforced concrete bridge spans
operating_conditions: Alpine climate exposure, de-icing salts, and heavy traffic loads
fault_modes: Concrete spalling, rebar corrosion, deck cracking, bearing degradation
rul_target_definition: Time to exceed critical reliability index threshold (beta_crit < 3.0)
preprocessing_and_windowing: Discretization into discrete Condition States (CS1 to CS5)
split_protocol: Calibration on historical visual inspection records; forward simulation of degradation trajectories
model_or_method: Non-homogeneous Markov Chain deterioration model coupled with structural reliability analysis
point_prediction_method: Expected condition state progression over 10-50 year horizons
calibration_method: Bayesian updating using periodic visual inspection likelihoods
uncertainty_metrics: State probability distribution entropy and variance
point_prediction_metrics: Reliability index beta(t) and Priority Index (PI)
degradation_stage_analysis: Yes, condition transitions modeled explicitly from intact (CS1) to failed (CS5)
operating_regime_analysis: Differentiated by environmental exposure severity and bridge structural typology
cross_condition_evaluation: Tested across multiple bridge spans in the regional network
maintenance_decision_layer: Explicit: Automated Priority Index computation to rank interventions under constrained budget
maintenance_cost_risk_eval: Evaluates cost-benefit of early intervention vs. delayed reconstruction costs

relevance_to_rqs: Directly inspires RQ3 decision-support formulation; uses Markov chains rather than deep learning time-series RUL.
evidence_strength: High (Rigorous engineering methodology with empirical field data)

title: Research on Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Equipment Based on Digital Twins
authors: Jiaju Wu, Yuanlin Zhou, Xiaodong Wang, Chuan Chen, Yongqi Ma, Chunrui Zhang
research_problem: Single machine learning models have poor generalization and low robustness for online equipment RUL prediction in Digital Twin environments
research_objective: Construct a Digital Twin-based RUL prediction framework using a Genetic Algorithm-optimized ensemble stacking method
dataset: NASA C-MAPSS turbofan degradation benchmark dataset
fault_modes: High-Pressure Compressor (HPC) degradation
rul_target_definition: Piecewise linear RUL with cap RUL_max = 125 cycles
preprocessing_and_windowing: Z-score normalization, 14 selected sensor channels, sliding window length Tw = 30 cycles
split_protocol: Standard C-MAPSS FD001 engine split (100 training engines, 100 test engines)
leakage_protections: Engine-level separation maintained in C-MAPSS benchmark
model_or_method: Digital Twin architecture + Genetic Algorithm-optimized Stacking Ensemble (Base: Random Forest, SVR, MLP, KNN; Meta: ElasticNet)
point_prediction_metrics: RMSE = 13.82 cycles, Score = 421 on C-MAPSS FD001 test set
degradation_stage_analysis: Evaluated RUL trajectory over engine lifespan, but no stage-wise metric breakdown
operating_regime_analysis: No (Evaluated strictly on single-condition FD001; did not evaluate multi-regime FD002/FD004)
maintenance_decision_layer: Conceptual engineering implementation plan for online maintenance triggering
maintenance_cost_risk_eval: None (No maintenance cost function or risk optimization modeled)
digital_twin_component: Explicit: Digital twin physical asset, twin data layer, online simulation model, and twin service application
statistical_testing: Comparison across individual base learners (RF, SVR, MLP, KNN)
key_findings: GA-optimized stacking ensemble achieves lower RMSE (13.82) than individual base models on C-MAPSS FD001 and integrates cleanly with Digital Twin telemetry pipelines.
authors_stated_limitations: Tested only on FD001 (single operating condition); did not test multi-condition datasets (FD002/FD004); computational cost of GA optimization is high for real-time edge updates.
authors_future_work: Extending to complex multi-operating conditions and exploring deep learning base learners in the digital twin pipeline.
our_methodological_observations: DIRECT CLOSEST WORK in local corpus. Demonstrates DT + C-MAPSS point prediction. Critically, it has zero uncertainty quantification, zero prediction intervals, no calibration, no multi-regime evaluation, and no maintenance-decision cost modeling.
relevance_to_rqs: Direct competitor for RQ1 (point RUL on C-MAPSS); baseline exemplar for what IntelliTwin improves upon in RQ2 (uncertainty) and RQ3 (decisions).
evidence_strength: High (Rigorous peer-reviewed experimental paper on C-MAPSS)

our_methodological_observations: Strong demonstration of using a Digital Twin to enrich machine learning data pipelines; addresses discrete anomaly detection rather than continuous RUL regression or conformal calibration.
relevance_to_rqs: Supports Digital Twin data synchronization concept for Phase 9; no direct bearing on RQ1-RQ3.
evidence_strength: Medium-High (Rigorous preprint / submitted manuscript with quantitative benchmark)

title: Data-driven predictive maintenance strategy considering the uncertainty in remaining useful life prediction

research_objective: Formulate a predictive maintenance policy directly optimizing expected maintenance cost by modeling RUL prediction uncertainty
dataset: NASA C-MAPSS turbofan degradation benchmark
fault_modes: HPC degradation
rul_target_definition: Piecewise linear RUL with cap RUL_max = 125 cycles
preprocessing_and_windowing: Z-score normalization, sliding sequence window length Tw = 30
model_or_method: CNN-LSTM feature extractor + Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) / normal error distribution assumption
uncertainty_method: Gaussian Process / parametric normal error distribution around point prediction
calibration_method: Parametric variance fitting (No distribution-free conformal calibration)
nominal_interval_coverage: Evaluated at 95% nominal confidence (empirical coverage dropped to ~82% on multi-regime FD002)
uncertainty_metrics: Prediction interval width, empirical coverage rate (PICP)

operating_regime_analysis: Tested on FD002 across 6 operating conditions, showing significant accuracy degradation
cross_condition_evaluation: Evaluated on multi-regime FD002, but did not evaluate cross-dataset transfer
maintenance_decision_layer: Explicit: Cost-rate minimization model comparing preventive replacement cost, failure penalty, and downtime loss
maintenance_cost_risk_eval: Explicit: Cost savings of 14-22% demonstrated over static RUL threshold heuristics
digital_twin_component: None
statistical_testing: Sensitivity analysis on inspection intervals and replacement cost ratios
key_findings: Incorporating RUL uncertainty into maintenance decisions significantly reduces expected lifecycle costs compared to point-prediction thresholds. However, Gaussian error assumptions fail under multi-condition regimes.
authors_stated_limitations: Assumes Gaussian-distributed prediction error; does not provide finite-sample coverage guarantees; computational overhead of GPR scales cubically with sample size.
authors_future_work: Investigating non-parametric uncertainty representations and multi-component maintenance optimization.
our_methodological_observations: MAJOR CLOSEST WORK for RQ3. Proves that RUL uncertainty improves maintenance cost over point predictions. However, its parametric Gaussian assumption causes severe miscalibration on multi-condition datasets, and it does not examine conditional coverage failures across wear stages.
relevance_to_rqs: Direct competitor and baseline for RQ2 (uncertainty) and RQ3 (decision cost).

title: Predictive Maintenance Strategies for Aero-Engines Considering Remaining Useful Life Prediction Interval
authors: Zhengbo Zhu, Lubing Wang, Mingchih Chen, Xufeng Zhao
research_problem: Point-based aero-engine overhaul scheduling fails to bound the risk of in-flight engine shutdowns
research_objective: Develop risk-bounded predictive maintenance strategies for aero-engines using RUL prediction intervals

fault_modes: HPC degradation
rul_target_definition: Piecewise linear RUL (cap = 130 cycles)
preprocessing_and_windowing: MinMax normalization, temporal sliding window Tw = 30
model_or_method: Quantile Regression Neural Network (QRNN) coupled with age-dependent replacement thresholds
calibration_method: Raw quantile loss optimization (No post-hoc conformal calibration)
degradation_stage_analysis: Partial: Examined interval width behavior in late-life cycles (RUL < 30)
operating_regime_analysis: No (FD001 only)

maintenance_cost_risk_eval: Explicit: Penalizes unscheduled depot visits vs. planned preventive replacements

title: Turbofan Engine Remaining Useful Life Prediction with Reliable Prediction Intervals via LSTM-Based Quantile Regression and Conformal Calibration
authors: Xudong Diao, Shaocheng Zhou, Fansheng Meng
research_problem: Raw quantile regression for turbofan RUL exhibits severe empirical undercoverage due to finite-sample estimation errors
research_objective: Construct reliable, finite-sample calibrated prediction intervals for C-MAPSS turbofans using inductive conformal prediction
dataset: NASA C-MAPSS benchmark
operating_conditions: Single-condition (FD001: 1 fault mode; FD003: 2 fault modes)
fault_modes: HPC degradation and Fan degradation
rul_target_definition: Piecewise linear RUL with cap = 125 cycles
preprocessing_and_windowing: Standardization, 14 sensor selection, sliding window Tw = 30
split_protocol: Training engines further partitioned into proper training (70%) and calibration (30%); tested on standard C-MAPSS test engines
leakage_protections: Engine-level split strictly preserved in calibration partition
model_or_method: LSTM-based Quantile Regression (LSTM-QR) + Split Conformal Prediction (SCP) / Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR)
calibration_method: Inductive Split Conformal Prediction with non-conformity score based on quantile residual violation
nominal_interval_coverage: 90% and 95% nominal confidence: achieved exactly >= 90.2% and >= 95.1% marginal test coverage
degradation_stage_analysis: Plotted interval trajectories, but did NOT evaluate conditional coverage (PICP) broken down by wear stages (early/mid/late)
operating_regime_analysis: Tested on FD001 and FD003, but did NOT test on multi-regime FD002 or FD004
maintenance_decision_layer: None (Purely algorithmic prediction interval paper)
maintenance_cost_risk_eval: None (No downstream maintenance simulation or cost metrics)
digital_twin_component: None
statistical_testing: Coverage probability guarantee proofs verified across 10 random calibration splits
key_findings: Conformal calibration successfully corrects raw quantile undercoverage (boosting empirical coverage from 84.3% to guaranteed 95.2%) while maintaining narrow interval widths on turbofan test engines.
authors_stated_limitations: Tested only on single operating condition datasets (FD001, FD003); conformal guarantee holds only marginally over the entire test set, not conditionally for every individual operating regime.
authors_future_work: Investigating localized conformal prediction for complex multi-condition operations and applying intervals to dynamic control.
our_methodological_observations: CRITICAL CLOSEST WORK for RQ2. Proves that conformal prediction solves marginal undercoverage on C-MAPSS. Crucially, authors note that marginal validity does NOT guarantee conditional coverage, and they leave multi-regime settings (FD002/FD004) and downstream maintenance decision consequences completely unaddressed.
relevance_to_rqs: Direct competitor for RQ2. Provides the exact empirical launching point for IntelliTwin's conditional calibration and decision-support investigations.
evidence_strength: Very High (Brand new 2026 peer-reviewed journal paper on exact turbofan benchmark)

title: Uncertainty-aware remaining useful life prediction and PPO based optimal maintenance scheduling in industrial IoT

fault_modes: Single and dual failure modes
rul_target_definition: Piecewise linear RUL (cap = 125)

title: Empirical Calibration and Conditional-Reliability Diagnostics for Bearing RUL Prediction under Operating-Regime Shift
authors: Yang, Wang, and Wang
research_problem: Marginally calibrated RUL intervals conceal localized conditional undercoverage when operating conditions shift dynamically
research_objective: Diagnose conditional calibration failures across operating regimes and propose group-conditional calibration for bearing RUL
dataset: PRONOSTIA and XJTU-SY run-to-failure bearing datasets
operating_conditions: Multiple discrete speed and radial load regimes
fault_modes: Inner race, outer race, and cage degradation
rul_target_definition: Normalized run-to-failure cycle ratio [0, 1]
preprocessing_and_windowing: Wavelet packet decomposition and time-frequency feature extraction
leakage_protections: Strict asset-level isolation across train and test folds
model_or_method: Bayesian Neural Network + Group-Conditional Conformal Calibration
calibration_method: Conformal calibration stratified by identified operating clusters
uncertainty_metrics: Marginal PICP, Worst-Group PICP, Conditional Coverage Violation (CCV)
degradation_stage_analysis: Yes, evaluated coverage specifically in severe wear phase
operating_regime_analysis: Core focus: Diagnosed that marginal 90% coverage hid a 64% coverage in high-load regimes
maintenance_decision_layer: None (Diagnostic and prognostic focus)
maintenance_cost_risk_eval: None
digital_twin_component: None
statistical_testing: Permutation tests for conditional coverage invariance

title: Conformal Prediction Intervals for Remaining Useful Lifetime Estimation
authors: Alireza Javanmardi, Eyke Hüllermeier
